julia_health_wiring.before: StudentTFit.nu_boundary was additive only (commit efe3d644): converged semantics unchanged, so a boundary fit could still present as converged=true.
julia_health_wiring.after: fit_studentt_gllvm forces converged = converged && !nu_boundary (mirrors _tweedie_verdict's :power_at_boundary rule, families/tweedie.jl), which flows into the GENERIC family-agnostic fit-health gate (sanity_multi / gllvmTMB_diagnose, diagnostics.jl) via fit.converged with no diagnostics.jl edit needed. Tightens the gate only; no existing pass case is affected.
julia_health_wiring.unit_test: GLLVM._studentt_nu_boundary and the conv && !boundary composition, test/test_studentt_boundary.jl
julia_health_wiring.red_first_fixture_test: pure-Gaussian data (test/test_studentt_boundary.jl, 'red-first: near-Gaussian data walks estimated nu to the boundary'; same construction as test_studentt_boundary_honesty.jl) -- asserts fit.converged == false, sanity_multi(fit).pass == false, gllvmTMB_diagnose(fit).pass == false when the boundary is reached

fixture_design.family_r: student(link = "identity")  (R/families.R:367-381; estimates degrees of freedom unless df is supplied)
fixture_design.family_julia: StudentTFamily()  (src/families/studentt.jl; identity link, nu estimated by default)
fixture_design.generator: tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.jl generate_fixture(rng): y_tj = beta_t + Lambda_t * z_j + sigma_true * eps_tj, z_j ~ N(0,1) iid across sites, eps_tj ~ standard t(nu_true) (Distributions.TDist)
fixture_design.design_note: nu_true = 6 is deliberately, genuinely heavy-tailed (not the pure-Gaussian construction used to exercise the boundary in test_studentt_boundary.jl / test_studentt_boundary_honesty.jl) -- both engines are expected to converge to an INTERIOR nu on this fixture. A local plumbing check (no real R; a synthetic 'R' file built from Julia's own fitted coordinates) reproduced converged=true, nu_boundary=false, nu_hat approx 5.89, sigma_hat approx 0.699 -- close to nu_true=6.0, sigma_true=0.7, confirming the fixture is well-conditioned and estimable at this size before any live R run.

quantities_compared: loading (per-species Lambda, sign-aligned for the K=1 indeterminacy)

both_engine_health_required.r: healthy == 1 (inline health check: optimizer convergence code 0, finite objective/parameters/gradient, scaled gradient <= 1e-3, sigma_student finite and > 0, df_student not at the nu_boundary_max = 1e6 Gaussian-limit boundary) AND nu_at_boundary == 0
both_engine_health_required.if_either_fails_on_this_interior_fixture: recorded as a finding in a-6-studentt-notes.md / the Totoro run's own output, never silently fudged, tolerance-widened, or dropped from the comparison (round2-3 #11's explicit instruction)

argv_convention.r_stage: Rscript --vanilla tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.R <data_path> <r_output_path>  (argv 2; K fixed at 1 in-script, not a runtime argument)
argv_convention.julia_stage: julia --project=. tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.jl <data_path> <r_output_path>  (argv 2; run once to generate <data_path> if missing, again after the R stage to verify) OR julia --project=. tools/core070_a6_studentt_fixture.jl --self-test (synthetic pair, no data/R required)

coverage_guard: the Julia stage refuses to report a pass while r_output_path is missing (exit 1, CORE070_A6_STUDENTT_AWAITING_R) -- a missing oracle side is never silently treated as agreement.
